extracted.intended_audience: GAP users; computational algebraists and programmers using the GAP system
extracted.subtask_description: Reference manual sections describing GAP's p-adic number support, p-adic extensions, MeatAxe module functionality, and tables of marks: definitions, function semantics, representation details, constraints, examples and warnings for correct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: p-adic family representation and precision
rubrics_metrics.description: A family of approximated p-adic numbers consists of p-adic numbers with a fixed prime p and a certain precision; the approximate value will differ from the correct value by a multiple of p^digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In GAP, p-adic numbers are always represented by such approximations, and arithmetic with these numbers is done at the given precision. p-adic approximations are ring homomorphisms on subrings whose valuation is bounded from below, so rounding errors do not increase with repeated calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PadicNumber (pure) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: PadicNumber(fam, rat) returns the element of the p-adic number family fam that approximates the rational number rat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: p-adic numbers created this way admit the usual field operations; examples illustrate behavior of multiplication, division and scaling at the declared precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Valuation(obj) returns the valuation (the p-part) of the p-adic number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also PValuation; used to get the exponent v in p^v * (a/b) where p divides neither a nor b.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShiftedPadicNumber behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: ShiftedPadicNumber(padic, int) takes a p-adic number padic and an integer shift and returns the p-adic number padic * p^shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pure p-adic number category checks
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPurePadicNumber(obj) and IsPurePadicNumberFamily(fam) test membership in the category/family of pure p-adic numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PadicExtensionNumberFamily construction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PadicExtensionNumberFamily(p, precision, unram, ram) constructs an extended p-adic field L given by two polynomials with coefficient lists unram (unramified part) and ram (ramified part); the polynomial given by unram must be a cyclotomic polynomial and the polynomial given by ram must be either an Eisenstein polynomial or 1 + x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP does not check the cyclotomic/Eisenstein conditions. It must be ensured that both polynomials are really irreducible over Q_p; otherwise the 'extension' may contain non-invertible pseudo-p-adic numbers. The extension is represented as Qp[x,y]/(h(x),g(y)), and every number is represented as a coefficient list w.r.t. the basis {1,x,x^2,...,y,xy,...}. The integer precision is the number of digits for all coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreducibility requirement for p-adic extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Both defining polynomials for a PadicExtensionNumberFamily must be irreducible over Q_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a defining polynomial is reducible (e.g. x^2 + x + 1 not irreducible for some p), the constructed family contains non-invertible 'pseudo-p-adic numbers'. There is no automatic irreducibility check in GAP for these inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PadicNumber forms for extensions and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: PadicNumber has multiple forms: (fam,rat) returns the p-adic for a rational; (purefam,list) returns p^list[1]*list[2] where list has length two and entries of list[2] are not divisible by p; (extfam,list) creates a number in an extended family where list[2] provides coefficients w.r.t. the extension basis and list[1] is a common p-part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It must be guaranteed that no entry of list[2] is divisible by p in the purefam form (otherwise precision will get lost); for extfam the list conventions must be respected to avoid precision loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision representation warning in extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotient representations of p-adic extension elements may make precision appear to 'vanish' though internally the number stores maximal precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the same element can be represented with different exponent offsets (e.g. [0,[1.2000,...]] vs [-1,[12.000,...]]). Internally numbers can have the full declared precision even if a displayed form shows fewer digits; be aware of internal storage semantics (exponent shifts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Padic extension membership checks
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPadicExtensionNumber(obj) and IsPadicExtensionNumberFamily(fam) test whether an object is an element of a p-adic extension or a family of such elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to verify objects are in the expected categories/families.

rubrics_metrics.name: MeatAxe action convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The action of the GAP MeatAxe is always that of matrices on row vectors by multiplication on the right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to investigate left modules you must transpose the matrices. This convention is consistent with GAP's convention for group actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: GModuleByMats creation contract
rubrics_metrics.description: GModuleByMats(gens, field) creates a MeatAxe module over field from a list of invertible matrices gens; if the list of generators is empty, the dimension must be given as second argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MeatAxe routines operate essentially on lists of matrices rather than GAP modules; created modules are records with components generators, dimension and field; once created their entries may not be changed. Submodules/factor modules are represented as induced actions (again MeatAxe modules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not access MeatAxe module internals directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though a MeatAxe module is a record, its components should never be accessed outside of MeatAxe functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided MTX.* accessors and functions instead of reading/writing record fields directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTX global MeatAxe selection
rubrics_metrics.description: All MeatAxe routines are accessed via the global variable MTX, which can be assigned to different MeatAxe implementations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each MeatAxe implementation is represented by its own global variable; assign MTX to select the implementation to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessors for module properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MTX.Generators(module), MTX.Dimension(module), MTX.Field(module) to obtain a MeatAxe module's generator list, action dimension, and field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions return the canonical information and should be used instead of digging into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreducibility vs absolute irreducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.IsIrreducible(module) tests for irreducibility (no proper submodules); MTX.IsAbsolutelyIrreducible(module) tests irreducibility over the algebraic closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute irreducibility is formally tested by checking whether L ⊗_K M is irreducible where L is algebraic closure. Use MTX.DegreeSplittingField(module) to get the degree of the splitting field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposability and uniqueness of homogeneous components
rubrics_metrics.description: A module is decomposable if it can be written as a direct sum of two proper submodules; every finite dimensional module is a direct sum of indecomposable parts; homogeneous components (direct sums of isomorphic indecomposables) are uniquely determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MTX.IsIndecomposable(module) and MTX.Indecomposition(module) to obtain decompositions (Indecomposition returns lists [B,ind] with basis vectors and induced module).

rubrics_metrics.name: MTX.HomogeneousComponents output structure
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.HomogeneousComponents(module) returns a list of records corresponding to each isomorphism type of indecomposable components; each record contains indices, component and images (with isomorphisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indices refer to positions given by MTX.Indecomposition; images is a list of remaining indecomposables each with an isomorphism from the defining component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submodule/basis finding routines and failure semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions like MTX.SubmoduleGModule(module, subspace), MTX.ProperSubmoduleBasis(module), MTX.BasesSubmodules(module), MTX.BasesMinimalSubmodules(module), MTX.BasesMaximalSubmodules(module) return bases for submodules or fail if none exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MTX.SubmoduleGModule returns a normalized basis of the submodule generated by subspace; ProperSubmoduleBasis returns a basis of a proper submodule or fail when none exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special submodule basis routines
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.BasisRadical(module) returns a basis of the radical; MTX.BasisSocle(module) returns a basis of the socle; MTX.BasesMinimalSupermodules(module, sub) lists bases of all minimal supermodules of a given submodule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition series and factors utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.BasesCompositionSeries(module) returns bases of submodules in a composition series (ascending); MTX.CompositionFactors(module) returns a list of composition factors in ascending order; MTX.CollectedFactors(module) gives irreducible composition factors with their frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normed basis requirement and NB variants
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'normed' basis means echelon form with pivots normalized to 1. Functions with NB suffix require such a normed basis; MTX.NormedBasisAndBaseChange(sub) returns [bas, change] where bas is a normed basis for sub and change is the base change matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using MTX.InducedActionSubmoduleNB or MTX.InducedActionSubMatrixNB the provided basis must be normed to meet preconditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced actions: argument and return conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.InducedAction(module, sub[, type]) computes induced actions on submodules or factor modules and returns results in a list (sub, quot, both, basis) where type encodes which actions to compute: 1=subspace, 2=factor, 4=full module on a subspace-adapted basis; if no type is given it is assumed to be 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basis given in sub must be normed; actions not computed are omitted so the returned list may be shorter; functions return fail if sub is not a proper subspace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module homomorphism basis functions
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.BasisModuleHomomorphisms(module1, module2) returns a basis of all module homomorphisms from module1 to module2 (matrices whose rows give images of standard basis vectors). MTX.BasisModuleEndomorphisms(module) returns endomorphisms similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These produce matrix bases representing the linear maps between underlying row spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism and automorphism routines
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.IsomorphismModules(module1, module2) returns a matrix isomorphism if modules are isomorphic else fail; MTX.ModuleAutomorphisms(module) returns module automorphisms as a matrix group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreducible-module homomorphism utilities and preconditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower-level functions for irreducible modules include MTX.IsEquivalent(module1,module2) to test equivalence, MTX.IsomorphismIrred(module1,module2) to get an isomorphism (requires one module be known irreducible), MTX.Homomorphism(module1,module2,mat) to verify and return a homomorphism given a matrix, and MTX.Homomorphisms(module1,module2) to return a basis of homomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsomorphismIrred implicitly assumes the same group is acting; Homomorphism checks mat defines a module homomorphism before returning.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTX.Distinguish usage
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.Distinguish(cf,nr) takes cf the output of MTX.CollectedFactors and tries to find a group algebra element that has nullity zero on all composition factors except number nr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to single out a particular composition factor when constructing minimal submodules, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariant form computation preconditions and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions for invariant forms apply only to absolutely irreducible modules: MTX.InvariantBilinearForm(module) returns an invariant bilinear form or fail; MTX.InvariantSesquilinearForm(module) returns an invariant hermitian sesquilinear form and requires the field order be a square; MTX.InvariantQuadraticForm(module) returns either the matrix of an invariant quadratic form or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: InvariantQuadraticForm behavior depends on characteristic: if characteristic is odd, fail if no nonzero invariant bilinear form, otherwise return the bilinear form matrix divided by 2 (may be antisymmetric); if characteristic 2, fail if no nonzero quadratic form, otherwise return a lower triangular matrix; error is signalled if module is not absolutely irreducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: BasisInOrbit for quadratic forms in char 2
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.BasisInOrbit(module) returns a basis of the underlying vector space of module which is contained in an orbit of the action of the generators; used by MTX.InvariantQuadraticForm in characteristic 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: OrthogonalSign semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: MTX.OrthogonalSign(module) returns the sign ε ∈ {-1,0,1} indicating embedding into GO_ε(d,q) with 0 for odd dimension and ±1 for plus/minus type, or fail if module does not fix a nondegenerate quadratic form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An error is signalled if module is not absolutely irreducible. The SMTX implementation uses an algorithm due to Jon Thackray.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smash MeatAxe (SMTX) availability and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard MeatAxe in the GAP library is based on Smash and accessible via SMTX; MTX is by default assigned to SMTX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual documents additional, more technical functions available in SMTX.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMTX.RandomIrreducibleSubGModule
rubrics_metrics.description: SMTX.RandomIrreducibleSubGModule(module) returns the module action on a random irreducible submodule.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMTX.GoodElementGModule
rubrics_metrics.description: SMTX.GoodElementGModule(module) finds an element with minimal possible nullspace dimension if module is known to be irreducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMTX.SortHomGModule
rubrics_metrics.description: SMTX.SortHomGModule(module1,module2,homs) sorts the output of Homomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMTX.MinimalSubGModules and related assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: SMTX.MinimalSubGModules(module1,module2[,max]) returns (at most max) bases of submodules of module2 which are isomorphic to the irreducible module module1; SMTX.MinimalSubGModule(module,cf,nr) returns the basis of a minimal submodule containing the indicated composition factor and assumes Distinguish has already been called.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMTX.Setter and SMTX.Getter behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: SMTX.Setter(string) returns a setter function for smashMeataxe.(string) and SMTX.Getter(string) returns a getter for the component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to access internal Smash MeatAxe components programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMTX.IrreducibilityTest and AbsoluteIrreducibilityTest semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: SMTX.IrreducibilityTest(module) tests for irreducibility and sets a subbasis if reducible but does not set an irreducibility flag; SMTX.AbsoluteIrreducibilityTest(module) tests for absolute irreducibility and sets splitting field degree but neither sets a flag nor tests it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These routines can be used both to test and to obtain additional auxiliary data (subbasis, splitting field degree).

rubrics_metrics.name: SMTX.MatrixSum and SMTX.CompleteBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: SMTX.MatrixSum(matrices1,matrices2) creates the direct sum of two matrix lists; SMTX.CompleteBasis(module,pbasis) extends the partial basis pbasis to a basis of the full space by action of module and returns whether it succeeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMTX internal flag getters
rubrics_metrics.description: SMTX provides getters for many internal flags/components: SMTX.Subbasis, SMTX.AlgEl (list [newgens,coefflist] giving an algebra element used for chopping), SMTX.AlgElMat (matrix of AlgEl), SMTX.AlgElCharPol (minimal polynomial), SMTX.AlgElCharPolFac, SMTX.AlgElNullspaceVec, SMTX.AlgElNullspaceDimension, SMTX.CentMat (centralising matrix computed as byproduct of AbsoluteIrreducibilityTest), SMTX.CentMatMinPoly (minimal polynomial of CentMat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These getters expose intermediate data produced by SMTX algorithms useful for diagnostics and lower-level operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of a table of marks
rubrics_metrics.description: The table of marks of a finite group G is an n×n matrix M whose rows and columns are labelled by conjugacy classes of subgroups Ci, where entry m_ij is the number of fixed points of H_j in the action of G on the cosets of H_i. The table characterizes permutation representations and compactly describes the subgroup lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rows/columns are ordered so containment implies i≤j then M is lower triangular; diagonal entries m_ii are nonzero (index of H_i in its normalizer), hence M is invertible. First column marks give indices relative to trivial subgroup; last row entries equal 1 for the whole group. The marks relate to numbers of conjugates and subgroup containment via provided formulas (e.g., c_ij = (m_ij m_j1)/(m_i1 m_jj)).

rubrics_metrics.name: TableOfMarks object representation in GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: A table of marks in GAP is an immutable object tom in category IsTableOfMarks with attributes SubsTom and MarksTom that encode the matrix of marks in compressed form: SubsTom stores for each conjugacy class the class numbers of its subgroups (positions with nonzero entries), and MarksTom stores the corresponding nonzero mark values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MarksTom can be computed from NrSubsTom, LengthsTom, OrdersTom. A tom need not store its group; if it does store the underlying group and bijection to conjugacy classes, normalizers and derived subgroup can be computed; otherwise some information may be undetermined. The filter IsTableOfMarksWithGens signals availability of generators/conjugacy class info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing TableOfMarks from group, name, or matrix and consistency checks
rubrics_metrics.description: TableOfMarks(G) computes the table from the finite group G (requires the complete subgroup lattice); TableOfMarks(string) retrieves a named table from the library; TableOfMarks(matrix) accepts a lower-triangular matrix/list of rows (with upper part omitted) and returns a tom object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computing from the group may require computing the subgroup lattice (potentially expensive). For matrix input, not every lower-triangular nonnegative integer matrix is a table of marks of a group; necessary conditions are checked with IsInternallyConsistent (70.9.1) and TableOfMarks will fail if matrix is proved not to describe marks, but returning an object does not guarantee it corresponds to an actual group's table of marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for TableOfMarks and lattice interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Several methods exist: if group is cyclic, TableOfMarks constructs the table using cyclic-group knowledge; if lattice is stored or group is solvable TableOfMarksByLattice computes marks from the lattice; otherwise the cyclic extension method computes table of marks and conjugacy classes together. Conversely, LatticeSubgroupsByTom(G) computes the subgroup lattice from tom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TableOfMarksByLattice for solvable groups or when lattice is available; TableOfMarks(G) will compute lattice if needed which may take a while for large G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing and display conventions for tables of marks
rubrics_metrics.description: ViewObj(tom) prints 'TableOfMarks' and, if known, the identifier or group in brackets; PrintObj(tom) behaves similarly but uses PrintObj for the group; Display(tom[,arec]) provides display formatting.
